cards.family: quotients by involutions; invariant theory; descent of curves/covers
cards.canonical: classical invariant theory and quotient geometry
cards.potential: Literature can generalize quotient construction, but fixed/boundary/source-lift accounting is object-specific.

cards.contract: Given an exact quotient receiver and rational-source lift discriminant, make the missing lift an iff square condition, convert to a simultaneous Kummer-style square system and prove forward/converse reconstruction.
cards.input: exact quotient receiver plus source-lift discriminant
cards.output: Kummer-style square receiver exactly equivalent to rational source lifts
cards.quantifiers: all quotient points on the retained open with boundaries classified
cards.strength: restores rational-source information lost by quotienting
cards.boundary: no cohomological H2 lift, marked Brauer, MW closure, rational-point classification or source lift without the square condition
cards.family: 2-descent and covering curves; Kummer coordinates; intersections of quadrics
cards.canonical: Cremona-Fisher-O'Neil-Simon-Stoll; Skorobogatov-Swinnerton-Dyer
cards.potential: Literature-grade 2-cover/Kummer formalism may expose extra Selmer/local conditions or a standard terminal model beyond the algebraic normal form.

cards.contract: When exact elimination exposes a reciprocal common factor in a completed simultaneous-square receiver, factor it out with explicit rational nonzero forward/inverse square-root scalings to obtain a smaller iff receiver and audit physical-chamber preservation separately.
cards.input: completed square receiver with exact reciprocal shared factor
cards.output: strictly smaller iff receiver with reconstruction scalings
cards.quantifiers: all nonboundary source/target points under stated scaling
cards.strength: exact algebraic receiver compression
cards.boundary: no receiver/point closure, physical descent when chamber fails, or new character/isogeny credit
cards.family: birational simplification; norm/square systems; invariant theory
cards.canonical: classical birational and norm-form manipulations
cards.potential: Mostly repo-specific algebraic compression; literature may recognize a standard quotient/norm model but is unlikely to strengthen the contract itself.

cards.contract: Exhaust all primes below an explicit threshold for an exact finite-field predicate; for larger primes use an explicit smooth bounded-genus auxiliary curve/family, a bad-point bound and a Weil lower bound beating it, yielding the complete exceptional-prime set.
cards.input: finite-field degeneration/support predicate plus auxiliary curve/family
cards.output: complete exceptional-prime set and a witness for every remaining prime
cards.quantifiers: all primes: exhaustive small range plus uniform large-prime proof
cards.strength: all-prime completion from finite census plus uniform point-count theorem
cards.boundary: not Q_p classification, global rational points/squareclass exhaustiveness, or large-prime witness without smoothness/bad-point proof
cards.family: Hasse-Weil-Serre; Aubry-Perret singular-curve bounds; Lang-Weil
cards.canonical: Weil bound for curves; Serre refinement; Aubry-Perret; Lang-Weil
cards.potential: Direct substantial strengthening is highly plausible: sharper point-count or singular-model theorems can lower the threshold, weaken smoothness assumptions or generalize the auxiliary family.

cards.contract: When a transform chain returns to an endpoint-like model, classify predicates as inherited/new/forbidden and require an explicit reverse/source adapter before re-importing source-only hypotheses.
cards.input: frozen source contract, exact transform chain and returned coordinate map
cards.quantifiers: every returned predicate used for credit
cards.strength: specialized anti-circularity firewall
cards.boundary: no endpoint/theorem closure or reverse population equivalence from equation similarity
cards.family: proof provenance / circularity control
cards.canonical: formal dependency discipline
cards.potential: Literature search unlikely to improve current contract materially.
